summary: Prelaunch review of the frozen snapshot identified by manifest SHA256 0492701e… (not a clean-commit review). The diagnostic harness is largely sound: rank masking precedes psana/MPI/CUDA imports; placement is nested, PCI-ordered and verified against actual device PCI ids and against psana's driver-derived peer count (discover_peers groups by hostname+PCI, so the _n_bd_per_gpu==peers check is meaningful); the explicit 6 GiB budget is a counter, not a preallocation, so the per-device headroom gate (peers*6+4 GiB) is consistent; event coverage/bytes/reads/histogram/batch-split/stream/drain gates are exact; cold gate runs after DataSource setup with owner-scoped fsync+FADV_DONTNEED+mincore; NVMe evidence resolves mount->md->physical NVMe leaves without summing md bytes, requires both drives active and idle-adjusted >=90% leaf bytes with NIC RX <=10%; Weka requires idle-adjusted physical NIC RX >=90%; counter brackets enclose the timing window; pilots are traced and full runs are asserted untraced; stages are private, job-named, 0700, on FFB and /lscratch only; owned process groups are stopped and confirmed gone before stage removal, and stages are preserved if the group cannot be confirmed dead; the manifest matches plan.matrix()/CONTROLS/RESOURCES; the 31-test GPU acceptance count matches the pinned test files; JUnit shows 42 passed/0 failed/0 skipped. One blocking finding: the 3-hour walltime is not reconciled with the campaign's own volume and ceilings (24 full 335.8 GB runs plus two 336 GB stagings with full-read SHA verification, 4 GPU-test runs, 6 pilots, 2 probes; 900 s per-case ceiling alone allows 7.5 h; the accepted predecessor budgeted 1.5 h for 8 full runs and one staging), and no in-job remaining-walltime guard exists, so a walltime TERM leaves no complete.json/audit and wastes the exclusive 4-GPU node. Several non-blocking lifecycle/provenance items are listed. Verdict: changes_requested; not approval to launch.

limitations: Static review only: no commands, tests, hashing or job submission were executed; I did not recompute any SHA256 and take the manifest digest 0492701e… as the candidate identity as supplied.

The native compatibility receipt at sim10-kvikio-bounce-20261113/attempt01/native-compatibility.json is outside the permitted read roots and could not be inspected; verify_manifest's receipt gates were reviewed from code only. I assumed the permitted pr-source root is receipt['source'].

Results of the accepted bounce-buffer campaign (per-run seconds, GiB/s) and the historical hardware receipts referenced in README are outside the snapshot and read roots, so the walltime finding relies on the predecessor's 1.5 h/8-run request and the harness's own 900 s ceilings rather than measured rates.
No live multi-GPU/NVMe execution exists; allocation-time GPU acceptance, storage qualification, pilots and per-measurement audits are inside the job by design and were assessed only as code.
AST/bash parsing and hash-validation receipts mentioned in the round context are not in the snapshot and were not inspected.
Scheduler eligibility (two --test-only estimates predicting Nov 30 for an IDLE node) could not be investigated with read-only tools; refresh availability and resolve before any submission.

Exact sysfs strings for the 036 NVMe model, link and NUMA node (SAMSUNG MZQL27T6HBLA-00A07, x4, 16.0 GT/s, numa_node 5) could not be verified; these gates fail closed but a mismatch would waste the allocation.

findings.evidence: run.sbatch requests --time=03:00:00 and RESOURCES/manifest pin time='03:00:00'. launch.py runs 24 full 100,000-event cases (335.82 GB each, ~8 TB total) each under a 900 s ceiling (launch.py:197), two 336 GB stagings that each copy and then re-read the full stage for sha() verification (launch.py:153-154), four 300 s GPU-test runs, six traced pilots and two probes. 24 x 900 s alone is 21,600 s > 10,800 s. The accepted predecessor (sim10_kvikio_bounce run.sbatch) budgeted 01:30:00 for 8 full runs plus one staging; scaled to this matrix that exceeds 4 h. No time budget appears in README/plan, and launch.py has no remaining-walltime guard before starting a case. On walltime TERM the finally block removes stages but complete.json and audit.json are never written, and audit() requires all 30 cases, so the exclusive 4-GPU allocation would be wasted.
findings.requested_change: Reconcile the scheduler request with the campaign: derive expected per-case seconds from the accepted bounce-campaign results (or state a defensible budget in README/plan) and set --time, RESOURCES['time'] and the manifest consistently (likely 5-6 h), or reduce the matrix. Add a guard in launch.py that reads the job end time (e.g. squeue -h -j $SLURM_JOB_ID -o %e or SLURM_JOB_END_TIME) and refuses to start a case that cannot complete within the 900 s ceiling plus cleanup margin, writing a truthful partial status instead of being killed. Re-snapshot and re-review after the change.

findings.evidence: Staging uses `with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=4) as pool: list(pool.map(copy, items))` with shutil.copyfile of files up to 73.46 GB. If SIGTERM arrives during staging (scancel, or walltime), SystemExit is raised in the main thread but the context manager's shutdown(wait=True) blocks until all in-flight copies finish, which can exceed the 120 s grace from --signal=B:TERM@120. Slurm then SIGKILLs the process, so the finally block never runs: private stages remain on FFB and /lscratch and cleanup.json is not written, contrary to README's cleanup-ownership statement.
findings.requested_change: Make staging interruptible: copy in bounded chunks checking a stop flag set by the SIGTERM handler, or use pool.shutdown(wait=False, cancel_futures=True) on exit and let the finally block remove the partially staged directories. Alternatively document that a cancel during staging requires manual removal of <ROOTS>/sim10-storage-gpu-<jobid>.

findings.evidence: In the finally block, `shutil.rmtree(owned_stage(stage, media))` is called per media without a try/except. owned_stage() raises ValueError if the stage no longer resolves or its mode/owner changed; rmtree can raise OSError. Either exception aborts the loop, so the second media's stage is not removed, cleanup.json is not written, and the original exception is masked.
findings.requested_change: Wrap each media's removal in try/except, record success/failure per media in cleanup.json, and re-raise after writing so the audit can see partial cleanup explicitly.

findings.evidence: Expected NVMe model 'SAMSUNG MZQL27T6HBLA-00A07', link width '4', speed '16.0…' and numa_node '5' are hard-coded from historical receipts referenced only by relative path in README (../sim10_single_node_scaling_20261113/evidence/44770441/hardware.json), which are not in the manifest or read roots. The gates fail closed, but a string mismatch (case, spacing, firmware-dependent model string) would consume the exclusive allocation before any measurement.
findings.requested_change: Freeze the 036 historical hardware.json in the manifest and derive the expected model/link/NUMA strings from it (or document the exact sysfs strings observed), so a reviewer can check the constants and a mismatch is a real topology change rather than a transcription error.
